items.summary: رسائل نارية للبرتغالي
items.body: رسائل نارية للبرتغالي أكد البرتغالي جوزيه مورينيو، المدير الفني لريال مدريد، أن فريقه يستهدف التتويج بلقب الدوري الإسباني، وليس الاكتفاء بالفوز على برشلونة، عقب الانتصار بنتيجة 2-1 في الكلاسيكو على ملعب سبوتيفاي كامب نو، ليقلص الفارق مع غريمه الكتالوني إلى 3 نقاط. وأشاد مورينيو بأداء لاعبيه، معتبرًا أن المواجهة كانت الأكثر اكتمالًا خلال فترته الثانية مع الفريق الملكي، نظرًا لقوة المنافس وجودة لاعبيه، مؤكدًا أن ريال مدريد نجح في التعامل مع ضغط برشلونة والحفاظ على هدوئه بعد هدف التعادل، قبل أن يحسم كيليان مبابي المواجهة في الدقيقة 87. وقال المدرب البرتغالي: "ريال مدريد لا يلعب للفوز في كامب نو، بل يلعب للفوز بالبطولة"، مشددًا على ضرورة مواصلة العمل والتركيز، رغم أهمية الانتصار، محذرًا من أن الفوز على برشلونة لن تكون له القيمة نفسها إذا تعثر الفريق في مباراته التالية. مورينيو ينتقد تقنية الفيديو ورغم إشادته بالحكم الرئيسي، انتقد مورينيو أداء تقنية حكم الفيديو المساعد؛ بسبب عدم التدخل في واقعة تدخل جواو كانسيلو على يان ديوماندي، معتبرًا أن اللقطة كانت تستوجب الطرد. وقال: "الحكم قدم مباراة رائعة، لكن (الفار) كان نائما في الدقيقة 60، وكان يجب أن تمنح بطاقة حمراء بسبب تدخله مع ديوماندي". دكة بدلاء تمنح ريال مدريد حلولًا إضافية ودافع مورينيو عن قراره إبقاء إدواردو كامافينجا على مقاعد البد…

items.body: ما هو؟ أعرب الإسباني بيدري، لاعب وسط برشلونة، عن حزنه عقب خسارة فريقه أمام ريال مدريد بنتيجة 2-1، في الكلاسيكو الذي أقيم على ملعب كامب نو، ضمن منافسات الدوري الإسباني، مؤكدًا أن الفريق الكتالوني لم يقدم المستوى المأمول، خاصة خلال الشوط الأول. وقال بيدري، في تصريحات لشبكة "DAZN"، إن برشلونة لم يظهر بأفضل حالاته في النصف الأول من المباراة، مشيرًا إلى أن الفريق تحسن بعد الاستراحة ونجح في إدراك التعادل، لكنه دفع ثمن عدم التعامل الجيد مع الهجمة المرتدة التي سجل منها ريال مدريد هدف الفوز. وأضاف لاعب الوسط الإسباني، أن برشلونة افتقد الإيقاع في تداول الكرة، موضحًا: "كنا بطيئين للغاية في الشوط الأول، وارتكبنا العديد من الأخطاء الساذجة، وأمام فرق كهذه ندفع الثمن". وشدد بيدري على ضرورة تحسين الأداء خلال المباريات المقبلة، رغم خيبة الأمل من خسارة مواجهة كانت تمثل أهمية خاصة للفريق وجماهيره، قائلًا إن اللاعبين كانوا يرغبون في تحقيق الفوز وإهدائه للمشجعين، لكن الحظ لم يحالفهم. واختتم تصريحاته بالتأكيد على أن المنافسة لا تزال طويلة، وأن خسارة الكلاسيكو لن تحسم مصير الدوري الإسباني، مشيرًا إلى ضرورة تجاوز النتيجة والتركيز على المباراة المقبلة، في ظل استمرار الموسم وإمكانية التعويض.

items.title: Why private equity acquisitions like the one that just claimed BioWare are so dreaded
items.summary: BioWare is just the latest casualty in a long history of private equity carnage.
items.body: The closure of BioWare has not come as a huge surprise. The LGBTQ-inclusive developer of Mass Effect and Dragon Age, which hadn't managed to transmute development mayhem into sales success and whose games aren't ideal environments for loot boxes, did not seem likely to be admired by its new owners, Saudi Arabia and Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner. Employees at the legendary RPG studio started working on their resumes as soon as the acquisition was announced. But even if BioWare's new owners had been miscellaneous investors rather than Saudi royalty, the outlook would not have been good: This is what private equity does. Public companies are of course plenty capable of blowing things up all on their own. EA's pre-acquisition attempt to turn BioWare into a live-service shooter studio was one of the great missteps of the live service goldrush, and Microsoft's pursuit of shareholder value has led to thousands of layoffs and numerous game cancellations. But there is a particular, systematic way that leveraged private equity acquisitions consume companies rather than nurturing them. items.body: One of the big topics of conversation around Onimusha: Way of the Sword when it released last month—and even before that, when Capcom first put out a demo of the game—was whether it was too easy. Viral clips of early game enemies standing around doing nothing gave the impression of a woefully easy game for action fans coming from the likes of Sekiro, Nioh or Ninja Gaiden. Once I played the full game, I found those fears mostly unfounded , but it's true that Onimusha's basic enemies pose little threat compared to its bosses, and mostly serve as fodder for you to cut through as you explore. Way of the Sword's harder difficulty option being locked behind beating the campaign didn't necessarily endear the game to hardcore action players, either, so I'm not shocked that one of the most popular downloads on the game's Nexusmods page is one that amps up enemy aggression . But I still mostly loved Onimusha , and didn't find myself craving the brutal difficulty of Sekiro or Nioh while I was playing it. items.title: Time could be running out for Arkane
items.summary: The famed immersive sim studio just got an extra month to find a new buyer, but will likely close if there are no takers.
items.body: Arkane Lyon may soon be facing closure, according to a new report by French site Le Monde , which says a deadline to find a buyer for the studio will land on November 13, at which point Microsoft could close the studio outright. Microsoft has since extended that deadline by a month, however, so it can continue to pursue alternative options. Arkane Lyon was caught up in this year's vortex of Xbox layoffs, announced in July , which will see roughly 3,200 people put out of work. Xbox also dumped four studios: Double Fine , Compulsion Games , and Undead Labs all went independent (and almost immediately laid off large numbers of employees) while Hellblade developer Ninja Theory appears to be closing outright. Because Arkane is based in France, Xbox couldn't just drop the hammer on it. Instead, it began a legally-required consultation process "to review potential strategic options." The Le Monde report says that on July 16, 10 days after the Xbox layoffs were announced, Arkane management informed employees that Xbox intended to close the studio. items.body: I'm always on the lookout for a new daily game I can play on my phone because, quite honestly, I'll do just about anything to delay getting out of bed for just a few more minutes in the morning. If you're into games like Wordle but are looking for an interesting new twist, here's a pitch: Wordle, but it's about pricing used cars Congratulations on your new job at The Daily Lowball , a used car lot where you have to prove to your boss that you know how much second-hand vehicles are worth. Each day in the puzzle, you're served up five real cars complete with photos and stats: the make and model, what year it's from, how many miles it's got on it, and how much it sold for when it was new. Now AMD's Travis Kirsch has spoken to Japanese outlet Tech+ about more of the thinking behind the re-release, and it seems the idea started at the very top. "Originally, several years ago, I believe Lisa [Su, AMD CEO] was one of the people who suggested reviving the Ryzen 7 5800X3D." "It was like a final gift to our loyal users who had used our AM4 for almost 10 years, giving them one last chance to upgrade their PCs using DDR4 systems," Kirsch continues. The company has been ruling the router roost recently and notably broke the 3,000 Mbps transfer-rate barrier with its AI-enhanced, ROG Rapture GT-BE19000AI Wi-Fi 7 gaming router. That’s old hat now that its functionally-identical Wi-Fi 8 sibling, the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 , is here. Or is it? Wi-Fi 8 (also known as 802.11bn) is expected to be officially ratified in late 2028. By the time you read this, at least four routers will have hit the market, but no laptops (or other devices) are in sight. But, that shouldn’t matter. We've spent some time in the last year testing top-tier Wi-Fi 7 set-ups, and seeing they can be faster than some 10 Gbps wired connections, so why do we need another Wi-Fi generation? However, unlike previous generations, Wi-Fi 8 isn’t about delivering more speed, it’s about delivering a more-reliable signal (including more-robust uploading), to new and old devices alike, in crowded Wi-Fi environments, over greater distances, in real-world environments. items.summary: Stuntboost is a racing game for FPS movement sickos.
items.body: Fast-paced. 3D Platformer. Parkour. First-Person. Racing. Those are the tags affixed to the Steam page for Stuntboost , a game that I've had trouble summing up with a clean label when asked about it. Stuntboost is a skateboarding game that sometimes features a car, a platformer with a speedometer, an ode to those shrunken bedroom maps popularized by early FPS modders. It's also, quite easily, my favorite game of 2026 so far. Yet, Stuntboost could've easily slipped under my radar. It's been out for a month and hasn't made a big splash on Steam—it's rated "Very Positive" with 253 reviews. I only found it through a friend's recommendation, and even then, the art style didn't immediately suggest it was my thing. Stunboost's toy fingerboards and cardboard circuits give the impression of a chill, Hot Wheels-adjacent racer your child could enjoy, but unless that child is accomplished with a mouse and keyboard, that ain't happening. items.title: A new Fallout 4 mod adds an entire town, but more importantly, it lets you join a gang
items.summary: They're not the Tunnel Snakes, but they're trying.
items.body: There's nothing I like more in a Fallout game then stumbling across some weird little settlement filled with oddball characters. So when I saw that this mod for Fallout 4 added a whole new town called Detour that's built on top of an overpass near Bedford Station, that was an instant download. Better yet, the mod features new quests and over a dozen new characters voiced by real people—no AI was used! But there's something better than that , even. I was delighted to discover that the town of Detour has its own gang . It's a small gang, sure: the overpass Detour is built on isn't particularly big and the town itself is pretty tiny, so there's not a whole lot of room for different factions to spring up. But that doesn't stop the members of the Detour Degens from occupying one little corner of the town where they hang out in matching jackets, smoking cigs, chugging from beer bottles, and looking tough. Sort of. Look, the Detour Degens are no Tunnel Snakes, that's for sure. But they live on an overpass. They're doing their best. items.title: Epic announces game jam where you have to use AI, then walks back the requirement
items.summary: The Unreal Engine and Fortnite company has extended the public a many-fingered invitation.
items.body: Unreal Engine maker Epic Games is running a game jam in November with thousands of dollars in prizes up for grabs. Contrary to so many art contests which ban the use of AI, participants in Epic's event are highly encouraged to use AI. The theme of the 2026 Epic AI MegaJam will be revealed on November 11, and participating individuals and teams will then have from November 12–15 to produce their games with the help of AI tools. Some will work in-person at a San Francisco event space, and there will be daily livestreams with progress updates. The winners in three categories will each receive $7,500, with smaller cash prizes for second and third place winners, as well as additional categories like "best team." Also on the table are "Development Continuation Grants of up to $50,000 per team." Epic extended the invitation with a reference to The Matrix's 'red pill' scene, presenting red-pilled AI-driven development as an opportunity to "ship awesome games in a weekend," while old-fashioned blue-pilled development would have you "wait months to prototype."
